job: Fix the production Shine V4 light-theme accent text contrast failure found by the Sergii browser gate without changing the page structure or dark-theme identity
primaryTask: Read and operate the same Shine page successfully in both dark and light themes.

defects.problem: Light-theme users cannot reliably read the lime eyebrow, version label, emphasized headline, architecture numbers, or workflow numbers.
defects.evidence: Fresh production axe reports color-contrast violations on 13 selectors immediately after the theme toggle.
defects.expectedEffect: All content remains readable and axe-clean after switching to light theme.

defects.problem: The production verification contract exercises the theme toggle but does not run accessibility analysis in the resulting theme state.
defects.evidence: The earlier measure receipt reported zero axe violations in the initial state while the new direct browser probe fails after toggling light.
defects.expectedEffect: The saved production receipt covers both interactive state change and axe in the changed state at desktop and mobile sizes.

defects.problem: One lime token carries two incompatible jobs in light mode: bright action fills and small foreground text.
defects.evidence: The action buttons need a bright fill with dark ink, while small text using the same bright value falls below foreground contrast on the off-white page.
defects.expectedEffect: Separate accent fill from accent foreground while preserving one coherent hue family.

defects.problem: The light theme looks intentional at a glance, which allowed the low-contrast lime labels to masquerade as acceptable craft.
defects.evidence: The screenshot preserves hierarchy and balance, but the smallest lime text visually fades into #f3f4ed and white surfaces.
defects.expectedEffect: Retain the lime identity while using a darker optical foreground value for text and focus treatment.
